unit: U1 (execution): replace.mjs, admit.mjs, stop.mjs, watch.mjs, status.mjs, handover.mjs

findings.claim: The memory reservation for admitted-but-not-running sessions (`pending`, M4) is computed in gatherFacts but no test exercises it: deleting the `pending += 1` for a row with no matched process leaves all 30 admit tests green.
findings.evidence: Mutation A5 (line 486 -> `void 0;`): node --test admit.test.mjs, 28 pass / 0 fail / 2 skip. T7 tests only decide() with a literal `pending`; no check/start test has an admitted row with a working process list and a --free-mb between peak and peak*(pending+1)+reserve.
findings.fix: Add a check-mode test: one row at active/admitted (no process, no transcript), candidate at active/stopped, thresholds reserve 1024 / peak 1200, --free-mb 2300 -> exit 6 with reason memory {pending: 1}; without the admitted row -> admitted.

findings.claim: Gate A as read from files (gateAFacts: approved ids of the current protocol, committed cards of the field, their last status, the latest pack's not_covered) is never exercised; only decide() is tested with a literal gateA object.
findings.evidence: Mutation A7 (line 357, without F5 a committed card covers only when its status is witnessed) leaves all 30 admit tests green. Any error in how gate A is computed before a review start would pass unnoticed.
findings.fix: Add a check --task test on a review row: frozen protocol with ids [a,b], a committed card of the field covering a (status pending, f5_given false), a committed pack with not_covered [{question_id: b}] -> admitted; remove the pack's entry -> gate-a-uncovered {ids:[b]}; with f5_given true and the card pending -> gate-a-uncovered {ids:[a,b]}.

findings.claim: The per-tick ce check of the default-mode watcher (R4: the ce check is the first act of every evaluation) is untested. With it removed, a quiet watcher of an old ce keeps looping, keeps watcher.lock and keeps rewriting watcher.json; it only dies if some new condition forces a ledger append (withRunLock then gives 64). The successor's watcher then gets 75 and its endturn reports watcher-missing forever.
findings.evidence: Mutation W3 (line 315 -> `void 0;`): node --test watch.test.mjs, 61 pass / 0 fail. T15 uses --once, where runWatcher's own checkCe (line 699) refuses before evaluate runs; no test raises coord.ce while a default-mode watcher is sleeping between ticks.
findings.fix: Add a test: start `watch.mjs --root R --ce 1 --interval-ms 50 --no-intake` on a quiet root (child process, killed by the test in after()), raise coord.json to ce 2 after the first watcher.json write, expect exit 64 within a bounded wait, watcher.lock released and watcher.json not written after the raise.

findings.claim: An owner resume cannot take effect while the two fails are still inside W_cc_ticks: every tick with runFlags.halted false and a qualifying cluster appends a new `halt` line, so the owner's `owner {act: resume}` is undone at the next tick, for up to W_cc_ticks (30) ticks. In addition the window relative to ticks_total (`tick - f.tick < wcc`) is untested: with it removed, two old fails 5 ticks apart halt the run forever, and every resume is undone at once.
findings.evidence: Code: `if (!runFlags.halted) appends.push({ kind: 'halt', ... })` (line 489); lib.runFlags clears halted only by a later owner resume (lib.mjs 3356-3357), so the watcher re-halts on the same fails. Mutation W8 (line 474, `tick - f.tick < wcc` -> `true`): the three T10 tests pass (the 40-ticks-apart case is caught only by the pairwise cluster filter, not by the window against now).
findings.fix: Append a halt only when no halt or owner-resume line is newer than the newest fail of the cluster (e.g. compare the cluster's max tick with the `fails` recorded in the last halt line, or skip when the last owner resume has a higher seq than the last halt naming the same fails). Add a test: fails at ticks 10 and 15, ticks_total 100, W_cc_ticks 30 -> no 26 and no halt line; and one with a resume after the halt -> no second halt line.

findings.claim: `stop request` confirms a stop at once, with no process list and no wait, whenever the target attempt has no bound session and no folder transcript yet. For a row fenced at step admitted (the typical memory park of the newest session, a cut or a drop) whose session the coordinator has already started but which has not yet written its first transcript line, or whose transcript lands in a project folder transcriptsForFolder does not find, the slot is freed (stop confirmed, state parked/cut/dropped) while the session runs. R9 (the design) asks for 2 delta of non-growth and R10 counts every live child, stop-unconfirmed included; the spec's request step allows this shortcut, but nothing observes it.
findings.evidence: Lines 283-309: `session = att.session ?? pre.tt.folderSessions[0] ?? null`; if null, the update sets stop 'confirmed', step 'stopped' and dispose() runs, without proc.list(). slotCount then skips the attempt (stop confirmed), so admit can start another session.
findings.fix: Confirm at once only when the target attempt was never admitted (no `manifest` on the attempt). Otherwise set step stop-requested with session null and let `verify` sample the folder's transcripts and the processes naming the folder over stop_verify_deltas ticks. At least, take proc.list() outside the lock and refuse the immediate confirm when attemptProcesses(list, {folder}) matches or the list fails.

findings.claim: Intake steps run through spawnSync with no timeout. One step that never exits (snap.mjs --new waiting on the network, a script stuck on a lock) blocks the detached intake forever; the watcher sees the intake pid alive and never spawns another (lines 560-570), and no class, incident or status anomaly reports it. Harvest, commit intake, witness, promote and tms then stop running silently.
findings.evidence: Line 817: `spawnSync(process.execPath, [...], { cwd: root, shell: false, windowsHide: true, stdio: 'ignore' })` without `timeout`; step i only checks `proc.alive(state.intake.pid)`.
findings.fix: Pass `timeout` (a new threshold, e.g. intake_step_timeout_ms) to spawnSync; spawnSync ends only its own child, which is allowed. A timed-out step (r.error code ETIMEDOUT or r.signal set) gets the same `incident` {class: not-run, detail: {script, exit: 70, timeout: true}} and intake continues. Optionally the watcher records the intake's spawn tick and raises an anomaly when it is still alive after K ticks.

findings.claim: The epoch comparison of the READY re-check (R7/M6: only a READY of epoch E wins) is never exercised. The test meant for it writes READY epoch 0, which the ready schema already rejects (epoch minimum 1), so deleting `v.epoch !== epoch` leaves T5 and T5b green.
findings.evidence: Mutation R2 (line 196 drops `|| v.epoch !== epoch`): 12 of 12 T5/T5b tests pass. ready.schema.json: `"epoch": { "type": "integer", "minimum": 1 }`.
findings.fix: In T5 use a schema-valid READY of another epoch, e.g. `{kind:'ready', task, epoch: 2}` in wt/<task>-e1/staging, and expect the stall fence to apply (exit 0, epoch 2).

findings.claim: The in-lock quiescence re-check of `raise` (no row reached admitted/started/bound with stop not confirmed since the pre-check) is untested: deleting the line that collects such rows leaves every handover test green. The spec lists this race as app-only (NA4), but it can be reached without a race through a seam, and nothing else guards it if admission is ever started while draining.
findings.evidence: Mutation H4 (line 322 -> `void 0;`): node --test handover.test.mjs, 18 pass / 0 fail / 4 skip. The pre-check refusals (T5, T7) are caught by the slotCount pre-check, so they do not test the re-check.
findings.fix: Make the gap between pre-check and lock reachable in a test (e.g. an exported doRaise with an injectable `beforeLock` hook, or a test-only env seam that runs a callback after the pre-check) that moves a row to admitted; expect exit 6 not-quiescent, coord unchanged, one incident.

findings.claim: Endturn's watcher check requires `watcher.lock` to hold the pid and start time of `watcher.json` (spec --endturn step 2), but no test exercises that part: removing it leaves T10, T11 and M1 green. Impact is small (pid plus start time already identify a live process), but a watcher that has released its lock and is exiting would be reported as running.
findings.evidence: Mutation ST6 (line 645 drops the wlock conditions): 4 of 4 selected tests pass.
findings.fix: Add an endturn test: watcher.json of this ce naming a live sleeper while watcher.lock is absent (or names another pid) -> exit 1 watcher-missing.

notes_not_findings: watch.mjs 349-399: on first sight of a task (or a new epoch) the calls already made are taken as the baseline (newCalls 0), so that tick counts toward hang even when the session made calls. Spec says counters reset, i.e. new calls = calls. With hang_ticks 10 this brings a hang at most one tick early; the builder declared it (build-U1b) and T2-T4 rely on it.
spec/admit.mjs.md T8 is arithmetically wrong (10000 - 8000 - 0 = 2000 >= 1500 is admitted); the test uses e_task 2500 and the code follows the rule. The spec text should be corrected.
admit/status/handover call lib.slotCount without {root}, so relative attempt folders are matched as substrings in command lines; this can only over-count (fail-safe).
handover init refusal coord-exists writes no incident line although the spec's Writes list says 'incident on refusals'; T2 does not ask for one.

verdict: All 262 tests of the unit pass (245 pass, 17 app-only skips). 40 mutations were run, at least two per script; 31 were caught. Of the 9 not caught, 2 are redundant with a check the tests do reach (R4: getObject re-hashes; S4: updateRow's CAS). The other 7 are findings: A5 (pending memory reservation), A7 (gate A from files), W3 (the per-tick ce check of a looping watcher), W8 (the W_cc window against now), R2 (the READY epoch comparison, whose test uses a schema-invalid epoch 0), and the low-impact H4 and ST6. Three behaviour findings beyond the mutations: the watcher re-halts at every tick after an owner resume while the fails stay inside W_cc (F4); stop request confirms a stop of an admitted-but-not-yet-visible session with no observation (F5); a hung intake step blocks every later intake silently (F6). No kill, no write outside the run root, no network call, no command built from untrusted text, and no wall-clock read where the design counts (the pause discount is the one permitted, one-sided use). The formulas checked by hand (memory, reservation, slots, soft/hard floors, zombie, W_cc) are right.
